subject: Quantitative Aptitude
topic: Data Interpretation — Table and Pie Chart Analysis (W12 B1)

questions.stem: Study the table and answer Q1–Q5. Five students' marks (out of 100) in three subjects: A: Math=80, Science=70, English=90 | B: Math=60, Science=85, English=75 | C: Math=95, Science=60, English=80 | D: Math=70, Science=90, English=65 | E: Math=85, Science=75, English=70. — Which student scored highest in Mathematics?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Math scores: A=80, B=60, C=95, D=70, E=85. Highest = C with 95. Verify: 95>85>80>70>60 → C is highest ✓. Trap: E=85 is the second-highest (students may confuse 85 with the maximum).

questions.stem: [Same table as Q1] What is Student B's total score across all three subjects?
questions.explanation: C is correct. B's scores: Math=60, Science=85, English=75. Total = 60+85+75 = 220. Verify: 60+85=145; 145+75=220 ✓. Trap: 210 = 60+75+75 (wrong, copies English score twice); 230 = 60+85+85 (copies Science twice).

questions.stem: [Same table as Q1] In which subject did Student A score the lowest marks?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Student A's scores: Math=80, Science=70, English=90. Lowest = Science (70). Ranking: English(90) > Math(80) > Science(70). Trap: Mathematics=80 (second lowest, not lowest); English=90 (highest, not lowest).

questions.stem: [Same table as Q1] What is the average score in Mathematics across all five students?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Math scores: 80+60+95+70+85=390. Average=390/5=78. Verify: 80+60=140; 140+95=235; 235+70=305; 305+85=390; 390/5=78 ✓. Trap: 80 = Student A's score (not the average); 76 = wrong addition (perhaps 60+95 counted as 150 instead of 155).

questions.stem: [Same table as Q1] How many students scored strictly above 75 in Science?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Science scores: A=70, B=85, C=60, D=90, E=75. Strictly above 75 means >75 (not ≥75). B=85>75 ✓; D=90>75 ✓. A=70, C=60, E=75 — E is exactly 75, NOT strictly above. Count = 2. Trap: 3 = includes E=75 (but 75 is not strictly above 75); 1 = counts only D or only B.

questions.stem: Study the pie chart data and answer Q6–Q10. A company's annual budget of Rs.20 crore is distributed: Salaries=40%, Infrastructure=25%, Marketing=20%, R&D=10%, Others=5%. — How much (in crore) is spent on Salaries?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Salaries = 40% of 20 crore = 0.40×20 = Rs.8 crore. Verify: 0.40×20=8 ✓. Trap: Rs.10 = 50% of 20 (wrong percentage); Rs.6 = 30% of 20 (uses 30% instead of 40%).

questions.stem: [Same pie chart] Which is the second largest expenditure category?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Expenditures: Salaries=40% (largest), Infrastructure=25% (second), Marketing=20%, R&D=10%, Others=5%. Ranking: 40>25>20>10>5. Second largest = Infrastructure at 25%. Trap: Marketing=20% (third largest, not second); Others=5% (smallest).

questions.stem: [Same pie chart] How much more (in crore) is spent on Marketing than on R&D?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Marketing = 20% of 20 crore = Rs.4 crore. R&D = 10% of 20 crore = Rs.2 crore. Difference = 4−2 = Rs.2 crore. Alternatively: difference in % = 20−10 = 10%; 10% of 20 crore = Rs.2 crore. Verify: 4−2=2 ✓. Trap: Rs.4 = Marketing's absolute spend (not the difference); Rs.10 = the percentage difference itself (not multiplied by 20 crore).

questions.stem: [Same table Q1–Q5] Rank the five students by their TOTAL marks. Who is ranked 3rd (from highest)?
[Same pie chart] If the total budget increases by 10% next year and the percentage allocations remain the same, how much (in crore) will be spent on Salaries next year?
questions.explanation: C is correct. New total budget = 20 crore × 110/100 = 22 crore. Salaries = 40% of 22 crore = 0.40×22 = Rs.8.8 crore. Alternatively: old salary spend = Rs.8 crore; 10% increase = 8×1.10 = Rs.8.8 crore. Verify: 22×0.40=8.8 ✓. Trap: Rs.8 crore = old value (no increase applied); Rs.9.6 crore = 40% of 24 crore (20% increase instead of 10%); Rs.8.4 = adds only 5% or wrong calculation.
